conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. Can you tell me what’s been going on?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, doctor. I’ve had terrible stomach pain, constant nausea, and I’ve been vomiting for days. I can’t keep anything down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And the diarrhea—how many times a day are you having bowel movements?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: At least six or seven, all watery. I was on vancomycin at home for C. diff again, but it hasn’t helped much.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. You were diagnosed with a second recurrence of C. diff recently, right? And you started the vancomycin taper?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I finished the high dose, but then started vomiting and couldn’t keep anything down. I feel so weak and dehydrated.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. We’ve started you on IV fluids to help with the dehydration. We also gave you some anti-nausea medicine and pain relief.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. The pain is still there, but not as sharp since the morphine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll keep managing your pain. We did a CT scan to make sure there’s no blockage or other serious issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Did it show anything? I’ve had so many scans before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—the scan shows no acute problem. No blockage, no infection signs, no complications from your past surgeries.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. But why am I still so sick if it’s not C. diff?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We tested your stool again. This time, the C. diff toxin came back negative.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Negative? But I was just on antibiotics for it. Does that mean I’m cured?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It means the active infection might be gone, but we’re continuing the vancomycin as planned from your last discharge to be safe.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, okay. So I should keep taking it even though I feel worse?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Sometimes symptoms linger even after the bacteria are gone. We’re also watching for other causes, but so far, nothing else shows up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little better. I haven’t vomited since last night, and the pain is more manageable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great progress. We’re going to try advancing your diet—start with clear liquids and see how you do.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I have water or broth? I’m so thirsty.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Absolutely. We’ll start with small sips and build up. If you tolerate it, we’ll move to soft foods later.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. The nurse said you kept down apple juice and broth. Want to try some crackers?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, I’d like that. My stomach feels calmer today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also got your stool test results back—no parasites, no salmonella or shigella. Everything looks clean.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So it’s really not an infection now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not that we can find. Your symptoms are likely from ongoing gut irritation, possibly related to your history of gastric surgery and C. diff.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my G-tube? Should I be using it for feeds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not right now. Since you’re starting to eat and drink, we’ll hold off. We’ll discuss long-term nutrition with your GI doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs came back. Your white count is a bit low, and you’re slightly anemic, but overall, things are improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that from not eating?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Likely, yes. We’ll keep monitoring. The good news is your kidney and liver tests are stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve made great progress. You’ve had no vomiting, and you tolerated a soft diet last night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had toast and applesauce—kept it all down. I only had two loose stools overnight.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s a big improvement from seven a day. We’re planning to discharge you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What about my medications?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll continue the vancomycin exactly as before—twice daily for a week, then daily, then every few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my propranolol? I usually take that for anxiety.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re holding that for now. Your blood pressure has been low. Please talk to your primary doctor before restarting it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I will. And if I start feeling bad again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If you can’t keep food or liquids down, or the pain gets worse, come back or call your doctor. You have follow-up with GI soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, doctor. I feel so much better than when I came in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did well. Keep resting, stay hydrated, and keep up with your meds. We’ll see you in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick check before discharge. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I walked to the bathroom fine and had a small breakfast.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your exam looks great—abdomen soft, no tenderness. You’re cleared to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you so much. I was really worried.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re glad you’re better. Take care, and don’t hesitate to reach out if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Have a good day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You too. See you soon.
